highlighted_projects.description: Researched and implemented an IoT-based system using Raspberry Pi and RFID scanners to monitor passenger counts on National University of Singapore (NUS) campus buses. jarvis_projects.description: The Linux Cluster Monitoring Agent is a Bash-scripted MVP designed to help the Linux Cluster Administration team at Jarvis automate server monitoring. It collects hardware specs and real-time resource usage data from Linux nodes, storing it in a PostgreSQL database running in a Docker container. Scripts (host_info.sh and host_usage.sh) capture static and dynamic data, respectively, with host_usage.sh running every minute via crontab. The system supports automated data logging, centralized storage, and performance analysis, significantly reducing manual monitoring. Git and Docker were used for version control and containerized deployment, ensuring portability and maintainability.
jarvis_projects.name: Cluster Monitor

Additionally, I created a System Requirements Document (SRD) for a mobile-first Retail Investor Stock Trading Application, detailing functional and non-functional requirements, user needs, and compliance standards. This project strengthened my skills in stakeholder communication, Agile methodology, SQL, and end-to-end documentation aligned with industry practices.

jarvis_projects.description: Developed a data analytics pipeline for the London Gift Shop (LGS) using Python, Jupyter Notebook, and PostgreSQL. The project ingested and transformed a historical SQL retail dataset into actionable insights. Implemented RFM segmentation, customer acquisition analysis, and sales trend visualizations. Utilized Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib for data wrangling and plotting. PostgreSQL ran inside a Docker container simulating an OLAP environment, and Git was used for version control. The solution supports data-driven decision-making in marketing and operations.
jarvis_projects.name: Python Data Analytics
